whatItIs.text: Noodles of rice flour and water, from vermicelli-thin to pad-see-ew wide; fresh ones are deliciously fragile, dried ones are the pantry workhorse.

historyNote.text: Rice noodles were invented by cooks from northern China who settled the south in the Qin dynasty and adapted wheat-noodle technique to the rice that grew there; in ancient Tamil country, strings of cooked rice called idi-appam appear in Sangam literature of the 1st century AD.

howToChoose.text: Match width to dish — vermicelli for salads and rolls, flat medium for pad thai, wide for stir-fries; dried bags keep longest, fresh packs are worth it for texture.

storage.text: Keep dried noodles dry and sealed; fresh noodles are perishable and go in the fridge for only days.

useItUp.text: Soak dried noodles in hot water until pliable, then stir-fry — boiling makes them gummy; leftover cooked noodles refresh in hot water and crisp into noodle cakes.
